questions.question: If the cost price of 15 shirts is equal to the selling price of 10 shirts, then what will be the gain or loss percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost price of 15 shirts is equal to the selling price of 10 shirts

**Concept used:**

SP = CP + Profit

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let CP of 15 shirts be Rs. 15x

So,

CP one shirt = 15x/15 = x

According to the question,

15x = SP of 10 shirts

So,

SP of 1 shirt = 15x/10 = 1.5x

Now,

Profit = 1.5x - x

⇒ Profit = 0.5x

Profit % = (0.5x/x) × 100

⇒ 50%

**∴ Required answer is 50% gain**

questions.question: The mean of 100 observations is 50. If one observation 50 is replaced by 150, then what will be the new mean?
questions.solution:

Mean (100 observations) = 50

**Formula used:**

Mean = Sum of all observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

Sum of 100 observations = 100 × 50 = 5000

Let the sum of 99 observations which were not replaced be ‘x’

⇒ 100th observation = 5000 – x = 50

⇒ x = 4950

Now,

Sum of all observations (new) = x + 150 = 4950 + 150 = 5100

New mean = 5100/100 = 51

**∴ The new mean will be 51**

questions.question: The mean of 25 observations is 36. If the mean of its first 13 observations is 32 and the last 13 observations is 40, then what will be its 13th observation?
questions.solution:
Given:

The mean of 25 observations is 36

The mean of its first 13 observations is 32

The mean of the last 13 observations is 40

Formula used:

Mean = sum of the observation/Number of the observation

Calculation:

Sum of the 25 numbers = 36 × 25 = 900

Sum of the first 13 numbers = 13 × 32 = 416

Sum of the last 13 numbers = 13 × 40 = 520

So,

13th number = (Sum of the first 13 numbers + Sum of the last 13 numbers) - (Sum of the 25 numbers)

⇒ (416 + 520) - (900)

⇒ 936 - 900 = 36

**∴ Its 13th observation is 36**

questions.question: A tank has two inlets A and B which can fill it in 12 hours and 16 hours respectively. An outlet C can empty the full tank in 8 hours. If all three pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, then how much time will it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 12, 16, and 8 = 48 units.

Net combined efficiency = A + B − C = (48 ÷ 12) + (48 ÷ 16) − (48 ÷ 8).

Net combined efficiency = 4 + 3 − 6 = 1 unit/hour.

Time taken to fill the tank = Total capacity ÷ Net efficiency = 48 ÷ 1 = 48 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by inlet A to fill the tank = 12 hours

Time taken by inlet B to fill the tank = 16 hours

Time taken by outlet C to empty the tank = 8 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time taken = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

*Note: Efficiency of an inlet is taken as positive and that of an outlet as negative.*

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 12
 48
 +4
 
 

 B
 16
 +3
 
 

 C
 8
 −6
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net combined efficiency = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B + Efficiency of C

⇒ Net combined efficiency = 4 + 3 − 6

⇒ Net combined efficiency = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank = Total Capacity ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 48 ÷ 1 = 48 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 48 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet vs Outlet Efficiency

An inlet pipe fills the tank, so its work (efficiency) is always taken as positive (+). An outlet pipe or leak empties the tank, so its work is taken as negative (−).

Leakage Problem Logic

A leak in the bottom of a tank acts identically to an outlet pipe. If an inlet takes x hours and an inlet + leak takes y hours, the efficiency of the leak is the difference of their individual efficiencies.

Pipes Opened Alternately

When pipes are opened in alternate hours, calculate the total units filled in a cycle of 2 hours. Be careful towards the end, as the inlet pipe might fill the tank completely before the outlet's turn comes.

questions.question: A can finish a piece of work in 25 days and B can finish it in 20 days. They work together for 5 days and then A leaves. In how many days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

No. of days taken by A= 25 days

No. of days taken by B = 20 days

(A + B) together did work for 5 days

Concept used:

Total work = LCM of the time taken by the workers individually

**Calculation:**

LCM of 25 and 20 = 100 i.e total work

So, efficiency of A and B is 100/25 = 4, 100/20 = 5

Combined efficiency = 9

Now,

In 5 days,

They will complete 5 × 9 = 45

So,

Remaining work = 100 - 45 = 55 

B will take 55/5 = 11 days to complete the remaining work

**∴ B completes the remaining work in 11 days.**

questions.question: If x = sqrt3 + sqrt2, then the value of x² + (1)/(x²) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **x = √a + √b** and the difference **(a − b) = 1**, then **x + 1/x = 2√a**.

Here, a = 3 and b = 2, so difference = 1. Therefore, **x + 1/x = 2√3**.

The shortcut for **x² + 1/x²** is **(x + 1/x)² − 2**.

Applying the values: (2√3)² − 2 = (4 × 3) − 2 = 12 − 2 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x = √3 + √2

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and 1/x = **Conjugate** of x (when difference of squares is 1).

⇒ First, calculate the **reciprocal** 1/x:

⇒ 1/x = 1/(√3 + √2)

⇒ **Rationalizing** the denominator: 1/x = [1 × (√3 − √2)] / [(√3 + √2) × (√3 − √2)]

⇒ 1/x = (√3 − √2) / (3 − 2) = √3 − √2

⇒ Now, find the sum **(x + 1/x)**:

⇒ x + 1/x = (√3 + √2) + (√3 − √2) = 2√3

⇒ Use the **Algebraic Identity**: x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² − 2(x)(1/x)

⇒ x² + 1/x² = (2√3)² − 2

⇒ x² + 1/x² = (4 × 3) − 2 = 12 − 2 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator of the form (√a + √b), multiply both the numerator and denominator by its **conjugate** (√a − √b).

Sum of Higher Powers

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2 and x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.

Difference of Squares Identity

The identity **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²** is fundamental in solving reciprocal surd problems.</p

questions.question: Name the leader whose opposition led to the disappearance of all hopes of compromise between the Congress and the Muslim League in 1928.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MR Jayakar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Civil Disobedience Movement** received a lukewarm reaction from several Muslim political organisations in India.
 
• Following the demise of the Non-Cooperation and Khilafat Movements, many Muslims felt alienated from Congress.

• One of the Muslim League's leaders, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, was willing to give up his demand for separate electorates in exchange for reserved seats in the Central Assembly and representation proportional to the population in Muslim-dominated provinces.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to detect cracks and flaws in metal blocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ultrasound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metal blocks **can be inspected with **ultrasound** to discover cracks and faults. Large structures such as houses, bridges, machinery, and scientific apparatus all use metallic components.
 
• The strength of the construction is weakened by cracks or holes inside the metal blocks that are not visible from the outside.
 
• **Ultrasonic waves** are allowed to pass through the metallic block, and the transmitted waves are detected using detectors.
 
• The ultrasound is reflected back if there is even a minor flaw or defect, revealing the presence of the flaw or defect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SONAR (sound navigation and ranging**) is a navigation and ranging system that employs sound propagation (typically underwater, as in submarine navigation) to navigate, measure distances (ranging), communicate with, and detect objects on or beneath the water's surface, such as other vessels.
 
• **An echo** is a sound reflection that arrives at the listener with a delay after the original sound. It is used in audio signal processing and acoustics.
 
• The persistence of sound, or echo, after a sound is made is known as** reverberation in acoustics.**

questions.question: In 8 years, Subhash will be 3 times as old as he is now. After how many years will Subhash be 5 times as old as he is now?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let current age be 1 unit.

Age after 8 years = 3 units → Change = 2 units = 8 years.

∴ 1 unit = 4 years.

To be 5 times (5 units), change from current (1 unit) = 4 units.

Time required = 4 units × 4 years = 16 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc51e59d8dd5df3bef9e16e1ceddb02298fc24e0715bf15a5b6ce14a6eb6cfc7.png] 

**Given:**

Let the **present age** of Subhash be x.

After 8 years, age = 3x.

**Calculations:**

⇒ x + 8 = 3x

⇒ 2x = 8

⇒ x = 4 years (Present Age)

Target age = 5 × Present age = 5x = 5 × 4 = 20 years.

⇒ Years required = Target age − Present age

⇒ 20 − 4 = 16 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Ages

Age problems are solved by translating verbal statements into algebraic equations where 'n years ago' implies (x − n) and 'n years hence' implies (x + n).

Ratio Method for Ages

If the ratio of ages changes over time, the difference between the ages of two people remains constant regardless of the number of years passed.</p
